source: The ordering follows the consequence of missing each kind of bill: what you lose, how fast, and whether it can be undone. It is the sequence non-profit credit counsellors and legal-aid guides teach — keep the roof, the heat, the car you work from, and the food, before the debts.
confidenceNote: A general ordering, not advice about your situation. Consequences vary by state and by contract — some states bar winter utility shut-offs, some leases have grace periods, some lenders repossess faster than others. Where a step says to call, calling is the advice; this file does not know your terms.
note: `tier` 1 is what you protect first. `recoverable` says whether missing it can be undone, which is the whole reason for the ordering: an unrecoverable loss outranks a larger recoverable one.

tiers.label: Keep first — losing these costs far more than they cost

kinds.label: Rent or the mortgage
kinds.why: Eviction and foreclosure are slow to start and very hard to reverse, and they follow you into the next tenancy.
kinds.callFirst: Your landlord or servicer, before you miss it. A payment plan agreed in advance is a different thing from a missed payment explained afterwards.
kinds.helpLine: A HUD-approved housing counsellor is free — hud.gov/findacounselor.

kinds.label: Power, heat, water
kinds.why: Reconnection charges and a deposit often cost more than the arrears. Some states bar shut-offs in winter.
kinds.callFirst: The utility. Ask for a payment arrangement, a budget-billing plan, and whether you qualify for LIHEAP.

kinds.label: Food
kinds.why: There is no arrangement to make with hunger, and a food bank is not a debt.
kinds.callFirst: 211, or your state's SNAP office. Using a food bank while you are short is what it is for.

kinds.label: Childcare you need in order to work
kinds.why: Losing the place usually means losing the job, and the waiting list is longer than the arrears.
kinds.callFirst: The provider. Many hold a place for a partial payment.

tiers.label: Protect next — these take something away

kinds.label: The car payment, if you drive to work
kinds.why: Repossession can be quick and does not need a court in most states. If the car is how you earn, it belongs above the cards.
kinds.callFirst: The lender. Ask about deferring a payment to the end of the loan — many will do it once.

kinds.label: Car insurance
kinds.why: A lapse is illegal to drive on, and the policy costs more when you restart it.
kinds.callFirst: The insurer. Ask to change the payment date or raise the deductible rather than lapse.

kinds.label: Health cover
kinds.why: A lapse turns an ordinary illness into the thing that ends the plan. Marketplace plans have a grace period if you get a subsidy.
kinds.callFirst: The marketplace — a change of income may cut the premium sharply, and that is a change you can report today.

kinds.label: Child support
kinds.why: Arrears are not dischargeable and enforcement is severe. The order can be modified; the arrears cannot.
kinds.callFirst: The court that issued it, to ask for a modification. Do it while you are behind, not after.

kinds.label: Credit cards
kinds.why: The consequence is a fee, then a report at 30 days, then collections. Serious, and slower and more reversible than any of the above.
kinds.callFirst: The issuer, and ask by name for their hardship programme. Most have one and none advertise it.

kinds.label: Medical bills
kinds.why: These are the most negotiable debt most people ever hold, they are frequently wrong, and paid medical collections come off your report entirely.
kinds.callFirst: The hospital's billing office. Ask for an itemised bill, then for charity care or financial assistance — non-profit hospitals are required to have a policy.
kinds.helpLine: Ask for the financial assistance policy by that name.

kinds.label: Personal and instalment loans
kinds.why: Unsecured: there is nothing to take back. It damages the file rather than the household.

kinds.label: Federal student loans
kinds.why: The most flexible debt on this list. An income-driven plan can put the payment at zero, legitimately, and zero counts as paid.
kinds.callFirst: Your servicer — ask for an income-driven repayment plan, not a forbearance.

beforeAnythingElse.what: Call before you miss it, not after
beforeAnythingElse.why: Almost every hardship programme on this page is easier to get while the account is current. The call is free and the worst answer is no.

beforeAnythingElse.what: Do not borrow at payday rates to pay a tier-3 bill
beforeAnythingElse.why: A card at 29% is cheaper than a payday loan at 400%. Missing a card payment is cheaper than both.
nfcc.org member agencies do not charge for the first session and cannot charge for a debt management plan you do not take.
